card.name: Software described as also able to do something
card.fires_on: Subject words or small words like it, they, also, can, both, all right before a verb saying what a software tool can also do. Seen in descriptions of programs such as Solr, MySQL, and plotting packages.

modes.label: Subject before 'can also'
modes.description: A pronoun or subject right after a contrast, leading into an added ability of a program.
modes.example: Solr is generally run as a web application in a web container like Tomcat, but<< it>> can also be embedded inside of an application

modes.label: 'also' before a verb
modes.description: The word also placed before a verb that adds a further feature of software.
modes.example: Although MySQL is primarily used with Linux operating systems it<< also>> offers support for Windows, BSD and UNIX

modes.label: Quantifier after can
modes.description: Words like can, both, all inside a list of tools that share an ability.
modes.example: Xpaint, a Linux drawing program, and GIMP, an image rendering program can<< both>> import and export postscript files.

card.writes: Pushes toward words meaning can, has the ability, or possesses a feature.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a software description where the text is about to say what else the program can do.
